- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term mean reversion.
- Overshoots after sharp price increases (e.g., 76.67 → 76.52) are common, indicating model fails to cap upward momentum.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends (e.g., 70s → 65s), showing poor sensitivity to sustained bearish momentum.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the true mean of recent 30-day history — especially when true values are clustered around lower end of history.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the first 10–15 days of forecast horizon, then corrects — suggesting it overreacts to recent highs.
- When true values are below 70, model tends to overpredict — indicating poor calibration for low-price regimes.
- Model underestimates true values when history includes a recent sharp drop — fails to anticipate rebound or continuation of trend.
- Forecasts show poor handling of “mean reversion” — often overshoots after a spike, then underestimates subsequent pullback.
- Model is sensitive to recent high prices but underestimates the impact of low prices — leading to persistent overprediction in early forecast window.
